title: Kan fibers and fiber invariance for right fibrations
statement:
Use simplicial sets, horns, quasicategories and equivalences of quasicategories as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. A simplicial map is a right fibration if every commutative square with left edge $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, $n\geq1$ and $0<i\leq n$, admits a diagonal filler. Let $B,E,F$ be small quasicategories in the fixed universe and let $p:E\to B$ and $q:F\to B$ be right fibrations. For every vertex $b$ of $B$, the strict degreewise fibers
$$E_b=\{b\}\times_B E,\qquad F_b=\{b\}\times_B F$$
are Kan complexes. If $h:E\to F$ is an equivalence of quasicategories satisfying $qh=p$, then its induced map $h_b:E_b\to F_b$ is a homotopy equivalence of Kan complexes for every $b$. Here a homotopy equivalence of Kan complexes is a simplicial map admitting a simplicial inverse up to simplicial homotopies, with homotopies modeled by product with $\Delta^1$. Empty fibers are permitted.

source.place: Corollary 4.5.3.31 with identity base equivalence and right-fibration vertical maps; Example 4.4.1.11 (01EW) gives their isofibration property, Corollary 4.4.2.3 (019E) gives Kan fibers, and Remark 4.5.1.4 (01DT) identifies equivalences between Kan complexes with homotopy equivalences. Read online 2026-10-16; 01HK read by direct HTTP after the web reader timed out. Not archived under literature/. These are Kerodon tags, not Stacks tags.

proof.text: For $r:X\to B$ equal to either $p$ or $q$, form $X_b=\{b\}\times_B X$ degree by degree. Every right-horn lifting square for $X_b\to\Delta^0$ gives a lifting square for $r$ with bottom simplex the constant simplex at $b$. Its filler still maps to that constant simplex and therefore lies in $X_b$. Thus $X_b\to\Delta^0$ is a right fibration. In particular $X_b$ is a quasicategory, since its right-horn fillers include all the inner-horn fillers in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. This argument is valid even when $X_b$ is empty.

source.place: Corollary 4.4.2.3: base change of right-horn lifting, written out.

proof.text: For any edge $u$ of $X_b$ and any $n\geq2$, every final horn $\Lambda_n^n\to X_b$ whose edge $[n-1,n]$ is $u$ extends by the right-horn lifting property of step 1. The converse assertion of [lem-cbc-equivalence-outer-horn-filling] therefore makes $u$ an equivalence in $X_b$. Now consider any horn $\sigma_0:\Lambda_i^n\to X_b$. For $i>0$ use step 1. For $i=0,n=1$, fill the specified vertex with its degenerate identity edge. For $i=0,n\geq2$, its initial edge $[0,1]$ is an equivalence by the preceding argument, and the first assertion of [lem-cbc-equivalence-outer-horn-filling] extends $\sigma_0$ exactly. These cases cover every horn in the Kan definition of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Both fibers are therefore Kan, including empty fibers, for which no such positive-dimensional horn map exists.

source.place: Theorem 4.4.2.6: use (3) implies (1) for each fiber edge and (1) implies (2) for the remaining initial horns; the dimension-one filler is explicit. This proves 019E.

proof.text: The given right-horn hypotheses include all inner horns. We verify the outgoing equivalence-lifting convention of [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation]. For $r:X\to B$ equal to $p$ or $q$, a vertex $x$, and an equivalence $v:r(x)\to b$, choose an inverse $w:b\to r(x)$ and its inverse-triangle with edges $01=v$, $12=w$, $02=\operatorname{id}_{r(x)}$, as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Lift $w$ against $\Lambda_1^1=\{1\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ with prescribed target $x$, giving $\bar w:y\to x$. Lift that triangle against $\Lambda_2^2\hookrightarrow\Delta^2$ with prescribed edges $12=\bar w$ and $02=\operatorname{id}_x$; their shared vertex and base edges agree, so the lift supplies $\bar v:x\to y$ with $r(\bar v)=v$ exactly. To check that $\bar v$ is an equivalence, take any final horn $\tau:\Lambda_n^n\to X$, $n\geq2$, whose final edge is $\bar v$. Its image in $B$ has final edge $v$, so the final-horn assertion of [lem-cbc-equivalence-outer-horn-filling] extends $r\tau$ to a base simplex. The right-fibration property of $r$ lifts this base simplex extending $\tau$. The converse assertion of the same cited node now makes $\bar v$ an equivalence. Thus $p$ and $q$ are isofibrations in exactly the required convention.

source.place: Example 4.4.1.11, with outgoing lifting written by right horns in dimensions one and two; the reflection argument uses 019F (1) implies (3) in the base and (3) implies (1) upstairs.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-base-change] with $\mathcal A=E$, $\mathcal B=F$, $\mathcal S=B$, $v=h$, $\mathcal R=\Delta^0$, and the base map selecting $b$. The point is a quasicategory because every simplex and horn map into it is unique. Step 3 verifies both isofibrations in the cited convention, the given equality $qh=p$ is strict commutativity, and $h$ is a functor equivalence by hypothesis. The two degreewise pullbacks in its conclusion are exactly $E_b,F_b$, and the induced map is the specified $h_b$. It follows that $h_b$ is an equivalence of quasicategories, including when its fibers are empty.

source.place: Corollary 4.5.3.34, as stated by the existing base-change node, with the base-change quasicategory a point.

proof.text: Unwind the functor-equivalence definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] for $h_b$. It gives a simplicial quasi-inverse $g:F_b\to E_b$ and equivalence edges from $gh_b$ to $\operatorname{id}_{E_b}$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(E_b,E_b)$ and from $h_bg$ to $\operatorname{id}_{F_b}$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(F_b,F_b)$; if either edge has the opposite orientation, take its inverse edge, supplied by the definition of an equivalence edge. The degree-one formula for the internal functor simplicial set identifies these edges with maps $E_b\times\Delta^1\to E_b$ and $F_b\times\Delta^1\to F_b$ with precisely the required endpoints. Hence $g$ and these homotopies exhibit $h_b$ as a simplicial homotopy equivalence. Step 2 already established its Kan source and target.

source.place: Remark 4.5.1.4; elementary unfolding of the project quasi-inverse and internal-functor conventions.

lean.statement: theorem rightFibration_fibers {B E F : SSet.{u}} [Quasicategory B] [Quasicategory E] [Quasicategory F] (p : E ⟶ B) (q : F ⟶ B) (hp : ∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 1)), 1 ≤ n → 0 < i → HasLiftingProperty (horn n i).ι p) (hq : ∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 1)), 1 ≤ n → 0 < i → HasLiftingProperty (horn n i).ι q) : (∀ b : B _⦋0⦌, KanComplex (pullback (SSet.const (X := Δ[0]) b) p) ∧ KanComplex (pullback (SSet.const (X := Δ[0]) b) q)) ∧ (∀ (h : E ⟶ F) (w : h ≫ q = p), IsFunctorEquivalence h → ∀ b : B _⦋0⦌, ∃ g : pullback (SSet.const (X := Δ[0]) b) q ⟶ pullback (SSet.const (X := Δ[0]) b) p, Nonempty (SSet.Homotopy (rightFibrationFiberMap p q h w b ≫ g) (𝟙 _)) ∧ Nonempty (SSet.Homotopy (g ≫ rightFibrationFiberMap p q h w b) (𝟙 _)))
